Carleo et al. 2020 (GAPS XXI, arXiv:2002.10562) is titled '...refutation of AD Leo b'; Kossakowski et al. 2022 (arXiv:2209.05814) and Carmona et al. 2023 (arXiv:2303.16712, 'no evidence for a corotating planet') agree. exoplanet.eu lists it Controversial. AD Leo has no other planet claim in either catalogue, so no new system is proposed.

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.topic: TOI-4353.01 period on the Unconfirmed tab is a duotransit alias
incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.detail: The sheet (and NASA TOI table) give TOI-4353.01 P = 718.1809317 d. Tschudi 2026 (arXiv:2607.23781, Sect. V.1 and Table 10) finds two consecutive transits 39.899 d apart (one in sector 97) and determines P = 39.8991 +/- 0.0003 d, "an exact 18:1 alias of the cataloged 718.18 d duotransit baseline"; Rp 1.4 +/- 0.1 Re (CHIRON-revised), FPP 64%, FLAG_LOWSENS; in the optimistic HZ. The existing row's period and a_au (1.1755) would change if adopted. The paper is unrefereed.

Tschudi 2026 flags 11 cataloged M-dwarf PCs as false positives; the per-TOI list is only in the machine-readable tables, which I did not open. Some could be TOIs on the Unconfirmed tab (hosts within 100 ly with M-dwarf TOIs in the paper include TOI-4353, TOI-6284, TOI-732, TOI-1231, TOI-4336, TOI-4529, TOI-4599, TOI-2267). Worth a check by whoever owns the TOI rows.

Of their 17 Gaia-orbit exoplanet candidates, four have parallax >= 32.616 mas: 5486916932205092352 (= Gaia-ASOI-037, already Rejected), 4188996885011268608 (= Gaia-ASOI-025 / GJ 773 Bb, already Rejected), and the two added here (5796338299045711232, 198464052134353536). 4842246017566495232 (Gaia-ASOI-031) is just outside at 31.33 mas.
